_comment: The band table for the three-band payload policy, read by BOTH implementations: scripts/_payload_policy.py (--selftest) and scripts/_payload_policy.js. tests/payload_policy.test.mjs runs each side over this table, checks every verdict against `expect`, and fails on the first disagreement between the two. It is deliberately a committed fixture rather than a literal inside either test: a case table that lives in one language is a case table that only one implementation is ever held to. Boundaries are INCLUSIVE on the safe side throughout - value == target passes, value == action warns, delta == delta_cap passes - so each of those has its own pair of cases one byte apart, because an off-by-one in a band is exactly the mutation a round-numbered table cannot see.

cases.name: under-target
cases.why: the silent band: nothing to say

cases.name: at-target-exactly
cases.why: target is inclusive - the target is a figure to be AT, not to stay under

cases.name: one-byte-over-target
cases.why: the warn band opens at target+1, and one byte is enough to open it

cases.name: mid-warn-band
cases.why: where neural.eager_gzip_bytes actually lives today: over target, far under action

cases.name: at-action-exactly
cases.why: action is inclusive - 'we take action when it reaches >400k' is strictly greater

cases.name: one-byte-over-action
cases.why: the hard band opens at action+1

cases.name: far-over-action
cases.why: the fat wire coming back

cases.name: delta-cap-under-target
cases.why: THE CASE THE WHOLE POLICY EXISTS FOR: 70,000 bytes in one step, absolute figure still comfortably under target. A flat action threshold passes this in silence.

cases.name: delta-exactly-at-cap
cases.why: delta_cap is inclusive: a step OF the cap is allowed, a step OVER it is not

cases.name: delta-one-byte-over-cap
cases.why: one byte past the cap is the whole difference between a step and a cliff

cases.name: delta-over-cap-inside-warn-band
cases.why: a warn band figure does not soften a cliff - the delta cap outranks the indication

cases.name: shrink-is-always-fine
cases.why: a negative delta can never trip the cap; shrinking always passes, as it always did

cases.name: delta-measured-on-a-different-figure
cases.why: first_hand's shape: the bands judge the full figure, the delta judges the analytics-free subtotal, and the two are not the same number

cases.name: baseline-null
cases.why: a delta check that did not run must not look like one that passed

cases.name: baseline-absent
cases.why: same, by omission rather than by null - the commonest way state goes missing

cases.name: baseline-is-a-string
cases.why: '330000' compares and subtracts differently in python and in JS - refuse it in both

cases.name: baseline-is-a-float
cases.why: bytes are integers; a float baseline is a measurement that came from the wrong place

cases.name: spec-target-above-action
cases.why: the warn band would be empty and every overage would be a hard fail - the old behaviour, reintroduced by a typo

cases.name: spec-delta-cap-zero
cases.why: a zero cap fails every growth, so it would be disabled within a day

cases.name: spec-delta-cap-missing
cases.why: the loudest way to disable the delta cap is to delete it; that must not read as clean

cases.name: spec-no-gate
cases.why: a metric no gate claims is a metric nothing enforces

cases.name: spec-target-is-a-bool
cases.why: python's bool is an int and True < 400000 is legal arithmetic there; JS has no such trap, so this case is really a pin on the python side
